stem: A circle has a tangent at the point C, parallel to the chord $\overline{AB}$. If m(arc AC) = $({=a}x + {=b})^\circ$ and m(arc BC) = $({=c}x + {=d})^\circ$, where each of these arcs is the smaller arc, find in degrees the measure of the arc AB that does not contain C.
solution: Since the tangent at C is parallel to $\overline{AB}$, the arcs between them are equal: m(arc AC) = m(arc BC).
The whole circle is $360^\circ$, so m(arc AB) $= 360 - {=m} - {=m} = {=ans}^\circ$.
notes: b-d=(c-a)x so x whole; both arcs equal m (60-85) so below 180. c-a is 1 or 2; c x<=54 so d>0.
